detail:
The National Institute of Mental Health describes research on women's reproductive mental health conducted through its Section on Behavioral Endocrinology, with scientists working to identify the causes of, treatments for, and genetic factors in several disorders, including premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). NIMH notes that its studies take place at the NIH Clinical Center in Bethesda, Maryland, and require regular visits.

NIMH describes the entry point into these studies as a brief telephone screening interview, followed by an appointment with a clinician. The institute notes that participants learn to use daily mood ratings to monitor mood, and rate mood every day for two months, with that information used to determine whether study criteria are met. Healthy volunteers are also described as playing a critical role in the studies as comparison participants.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about premenstrual dysphoric disorder research and studies.
summary: NIMH describes its PMDD research program, in which scientists study causes, treatments, and genetic factors, using daily mood ratings over two months to determine study eligibility.
takeaways: NIMH studies PMDD causes, treatments, and genetic factors
daily mood ratings over two months help determine study eligibility
studies take place at the NIH Clinical Center in Bethesda, Maryland
title: PMDD (Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder): NIMH studies of causes and genetics
